findings.summary: Three consecutive main ci runs went red on e2e flakes, and nothing in the repo records them. [firefox] source-view.two-way-sync.spec.ts:201 failed at 94e0654, and [webkit] clipboard.cross-document.spec.ts:65 'the keys still paste in another tab' failed at 19447ab and b8f54c7. Rule 19 says a flake is fixed or quarantined, with a row, within 24 h. No row, progress entry or blockedReason clause names either test. ac27cb1 and fc0ef8a, both harness-only, landed about 1.5 h after flake-report failed and before any newer green existed. Under last-ci's rules main was red at that point (exit 1, no blocks-landing row open), and drive step 3 says the red is fixed first. Once 76c2e40's green arrived, last-ci stopped naming those runs, so only a record can keep them visible now.
findings.evidence: Here is what each e2e-report job printed. Job 126064075211 (ci 41624941136, 94e0654): 'flake-report: 936 run, 1 flaky, 0 failed', then 'FLAKY [firefox] source-view.two-way-sync.spec.ts ... a shape dragged on the canvas writes its pin, in one regenerated text' with 'retry 0 (failed): expect(received).toHaveLength(expected) Expected length: 1 Received length: 2' at :201. Job 126068174679 (ci 41625372038, 19447ab) and job 126083847570 (ci 41625760874, b8f54c7) each printed 'FLAKY [webkit] clipboard.cross-document.spec.ts ... the keys still paste in another tab — quarantine within 24 h with a backlog row (testing.md rule 19)', with 'retry 0 (failed): expect(locator).toHaveCount(expected) ... Expected: 3 Received: 0' at :65:35. Those jobs failed at 20:40-20:42Z. ci-ok concluded the runs at 21:57, 21:58 and 22:23Z. The ci runs for ac27cb1 and fc0ef8a were created at 22:15:05Z and 22:18:47Z, when the newest completed ci was 41625372038 (red). The next completed green, 41627122928, came at 22:27Z. playwright.config.ts:14 sets 'retries: 1'. `grep` for source-view.two-way-sync, cross-document.spec.ts:65 and 'the keys still paste in another tab' finds nothing in .harness/progress.md or docs/backlog/current.md after 2026-11-02. Both webkit flakes ran on code before c790660, in e2e shards between 16:46 and 17:19Z, while the queue was loaded. All six e2e-report runs after c790660 had no flaky test: 41633787769, 41638116368, 41639993998, 41640611038, 41660137068 and 41675824973. The test at :65 dates from e06dbd7 (M18.132), and c790660 changed both the spec file and the paste path it covers. Whether that removed the cause is not shown. A first try of 0 of 3 means no paste happened at all, which looks like a focus or timing race at bringToFront rather than a payload problem. The firefox case is the M12 drag-pin debounce, which yields two regenerated texts when drag frames on a loaded runner arrive more than 50 ms apart.
findings.failure_scenario: The 24 h of rule 19 run out at about 20:40Z on 2026-11-04 with nobody owning either test. The next flake on main, which is likely on a loaded runner, reddens a run that a held product stack then lands on. last-ci reads that red as the stack's fault, and a Fixes-ci chase starts for a race that was first seen and dropped here. In the webkit case, M18.242's closing evidence is the cross-document paste on WebKit. A known intermittent miss in the same spec would let a real regression of the ADR-0213 path pass as 'the flaky one'.

findings.summary: Over seven commits, M18.253's rule 'land no commit outside HARNESS_PATHS while last-ci exits 3' was broken once, by 76c2e40. That commit changes ADR-0020 and ADR-0213 under docs/architecture/decisions, which is not on HARNESS_PATHS, for feature row M18.242. The row also contradicts itself, because its own clause asks for Fixes-ci commits, which touch product paths (f0e2efc), docs/standards (0fc624a) and docs/architecture (0fc624a). Its bookkeeping clauses are still undone: the stale M18.205 clause, the ci backlog, and Huy's pending card on cancelling the nightlies. c790660's ci has now completed and needs its by-job record.
findings.evidence: `git show --stat 76c2e40` lists docs/architecture/decisions/ADR-0020-clipboard-format.md, ADR-0213-...md and docs/architecture/decisions/README.md. scripts/gates/landing-block.mjs:14-30 lists HARNESS_PATHS, and docs/ appears there only as docs/backlog/, docs/milestones/ and docs/harness/. At 12:59Z no main ci run had completed since 41595947349 (07:50Z), and none had a failed job yet (the first, 41628401301's macOS verify, failed at 13:41Z), so last-ci exited 3. same-tree.mjs:17 treats docs/ as non-product, so the two gate scripts already disagree on whether a docs commit counts. The state.json blockedReason is the same string in all seven commits. 41633787769 completed at 22:29Z. Its only non-success jobs were verify (macos-latest), cancelled by GitHub capacity, and ci-ok as a consequence.
findings.failure_scenario: The next driver reads M18.253 literally and holds a needed Fixes-ci because it touches docs/standards. Or it reads the exceptions loosely and lands ADR or other product docs under exit 3, as 76c2e40 did. Meanwhile blockedReason keeps telling a fresh session that M18.205 is waiting on M18.243, and says nothing about why ci is hours behind.

GitHub's macOS arm64 capacity cancels queued macOS jobs, and those runs then end red through ci-ok with no code cause. The nightlies' queued jobs are all on ubuntu-latest. A Fixes-ci row marked done before its run reads green would let a fix that does not work on the target OS close the row, and only a later, unrelated record would catch it.

questions.coherence: Coherent. The delta is CI recovery done in the right order. Two real reds got Fixes-ci rows with measured causes: macOS headroom via LETTERS, and Windows wall time via the job split. One reading tool (--show) unblocked two evidence rows, and those rows were closed from its output. The cp38 docs amendment landed as asked. Nothing contradicts earlier work. --show keeps its lines off the warning prefix and is pinned by a test, and ladder-split is one small pure module with tests.
questions.specFidelity: M18.247 is fully met, with every named case in ms in five runs. M18.248 is met in intent (see reviewedDelta). M18.255's fix is exact to its row, but the row was closed early (F4). M18.256 meets its first-record clause (a37e18c), and its fix is under the bound in both post-split runs (928 s, 607 s), correctly still todo. M18.242's docs clause is met. M18.253 is unworked (F2). No requirement was silently dropped. The flake rule (testing.md 19) was not applied to three main reds (F1).
questions.standardsDrift: The zero-flake rule was skipped for the first time in this milestone's recent record (F1). The drive step-3 exit-1 rule was not applied to two harness-only commits that landed on a red main, and the M18.253 exit-3 rule was broken once, by a docs commit (F2). Bookkeeping is otherwise consistent: Commit cells are filled, the header count matches 239 rows, `updated` is monotonic, and review rounds are recorded, including a changes-requested round (76c2e40).
questions.gateHonesty: m18-complete is 60/76 and cannot go green, with 22 rows todo, no mutation evidence, quarantine rules 19 and 20 in force, and no final review. ADR-0214 is not a weakening: no leg is dropped, each leg runs exactly once across the two jobs, there is no retry and no raised bound, and ci-ok needs the new job while all-green fails a skipped or cancelled job. Three mutants checked: dropping harness-windows from needs fails ci-workflow.test (`needs: [verify, harness-windows, `). Making --skip leave a leg unrun in both jobs fails ladder-split.test's exactly-once loop. Widening the Windows step to '--skip harness-tests,test' fails the exact-match regexes in ci-workflow.test and ladder-scope.test. One honest limit: last-ci forgets a flake once a newer green replaces its run, so the zero-flake rule depends on a same-day record (F1).
questions.architecture: Clean. There are no package or layering changes. The only product-code change in the delta is a test file. ladder-split.mjs and test-headroom's `shown` are pure functions behind the CLI. ADR-0214 amends ADR-0197 deliberately and updates ci-cd.md. Layering has 0 violations.
questions.planHealth: 239 rows against 43 planned (5.6x), up 4 since cp38 with 3 closed. For three checkpoints, every new row has been CI recovery or evidence, and the product stack (M18.35, M18.239, M18.130, M18.122, M18.250-252, M18.233, M18.147) has been held behind main ci. The milestone still converges. The remaining work is known and bounded, and the bottleneck is runner throughput, not design. That holds only if the pool frees (F3, Huy's card) and the flakes get an owner (F1). Otherwise every checkpoint adds recovery rows as fast as it closes them.
